The prompt for Job Descriptions:
For this Job Description: Paste job description

You are a resume tailoring analyst. I'm giving you my resume and ONE job description I'm applying to. Pull the keywords that matter for tailoring this resume to this specific job. This is analysis only do NOT rewrite my resume.

{how_ats_works}

- ATS parses sections (summary, skills, experience) and matches the JD's weighted requirements. Required qualifications matter most; preferred/nice-to-have matter less.

- Modern ATS accept semantic equivalents, terms do NOT need to appear verbatimto count. "Drove sprint planning" can satisfy "sprint facilitation."

- Keyword stuffing and unnatural comma-list padding hurt readability and recruiter trust. One natural mention in the right section beats repetition.

- So the goal is real coverage of what the role needs, not exact-string mirroring.

{how_ats_works}

STEP 1 — Frame it

State the role as "Title @ Company." In one line, give a rough read of how well

the resume already aligns with this JD (strong / partial / weak).

STEP 2 — What the JD actually wants

List the JD's key requirements as keywords/terms, separated into:

- Required (must-haves, stated as required qualifications)

- Preferred (nice-to-haves)

Order each by how central it is to the role.

STEP 3 — Already covered

Keywords/terms the JD wants that the resume ALREADY supports, including via

semantic equivalents, not just exact matches. For each, note briefly where the resume shows it. Split into:

- Exact-match terms (the resume uses the same named tool/framework/cert)

- Covered by equivalent (the resume shows the skill under different wording)


STEP 3 is the answer to "what do I already have." STEP 4 is "what to change."

STEP 4 — Tailoring opportunities

JD keywords NOT currently surfaced in the resume that the candidate can plausibly defend, because the resume shows an adjacent or same-category skill. Then also list out the skills or keywords that are not listed and would be harder to defend, this will be up to the discretion of the applier.

Rank the defensible opportunities by priority, highest first. Priority = how central the term is to the role × how easily the resume can defend it. This way, if there's only time for a couple of edits, I know which to make first.

OUTPUT

1. Role label + alignment read

2. JD requirements (Required / Preferred)

3. Already covered (exact-match / covered by equivalent)

4. Tailoring opportunities (with the evidence that justifies each)
